title: What If You Stood by the Most Radioactive Lake on Earth?

scenes.text: What if you stood beside the most radioactive lake on Earth for one hour?
Lake Karachay sits inside Mayak, a Russian nuclear complex that stayed secret until 1990.
Decades of dumped waste went into it. In the early 1990s, an hour on its shore meant about 600 roentgen.
Sources call that more than enough to kill you.
So the lake itself was the problem. Its radioactive mud could blow off the shore as dust.
The fix was to fill it in with concrete. A lake so contaminated that the answer was to bury it.
